body.cap: AVING News conducted an interview with HyeLim Lee, CEO of Kizling, at the AVING Media Stage set up in the Seoul Pavilion at Eureka Park, Venetian Expo, CES 2026. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Kizling Inc. (CEO HyeLim Lee) participated in CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and technology exhibition, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time), and took part in an interview at the AVING Media Stage inside the Seoul Pavilion during the exhibition period.

Founded in 2022, Kizling is a Korean software company focused on developing digital platforms for the Alpha Generation, including children and teenagers. According to the company, it invests its capabilities not merely in supplying technology and platforms, but in helping future generations experience digital environments in safe and creative ways.

Through this approach, Kizling aims to realize both educational value and social responsibility, while also striving to build an ecosystem that balances content creation and consumption. The platform, which shares the same name as the company, emphasizes moving beyond a one-way consumption model to enable users to become creators, communicate with peers, and develop self-expression skills.

Positioned as a short-form content platform dedicated to the Alpha Generation, Kizling drew attention from global visitors at CES 2026, showcasing its flagship service. The platform encourages children’s participation by providing a space to share short, intuitive videos. Its child-friendly interface and easy user experience also help lower barriers to entry for creative activities.

At the same time, advanced AI algorithms curate content tailored to users’ preferences and interests, while safety filtering technology effectively blocks exposure to harmful content, enhancing overall platform safety.

Furthermore, Kizling is a SaaS designed to allow teachers and professionals to monitor students’ video activities and provide feedback. The company actively leverages this service structure to continue collaborating with educational institutions and various associations and organizations, and to consecutively host new challenges and competitions for children on its platform.

The platform also enables children to share the content they create with peer groups and engage in interaction based on that content, fostering collaboration and empathy. As a result of being recognized for its value as a safe and organic digital creation environment and a digital literacy education platform, Kizling was honored with a CES 2026 Innovation Award.

HyeLim Lee, CEO of Kizling, said, “By participating in CES 2026, we had the opportunity to directly present Kizling’s vision on the global stage, and we were also able to meet many global buyers and investors who resonate with our direction.” She added, “Building on the positive feedback confirmed at the exhibition, we plan to pursue entry into global edtech markets, including North America and Europe.”

The company participated in CES 2026, held from January 6 to 9, as part of the Seoul Pavilion located in Eureka Park, the startup-focused exhibition area. The Seoul Pavilion at CES 2026 supported a total of 70 startups with participation from 19 startup support organizations based in Seoul, including the Seoul Business Agency, district offices, related institutions, and universities. The 70 exhibiting companies were composed of startups offering products and services based on advanced technologies such as AI, mobility, and healthcare. Among them, selected outstanding companies were given the opportunity to participate in CES’s official media event, Unveiled.
